what_it_does: Non-volatile memory (permanent storage that persists when power is off) used in secure systems must verify data integrity using cryptographic techniques. Traditional Merkle tree integrity verification is expensive because every memory write requires updating many nodes in a tree structure, causing latency and performance penalties. This paper proposes Adaptive Bonsai Merkle Forests, an extension of Merkle trees that reduces verification costs by identifying intermediate nodes as additional verification roots.
